text:
Roe v. Wade is controversial because it turned a deeply contested moral question, when human life or personhood begins and how to weigh it against a woman's bodily autonomy, into a nationwide constitutional rule. It did so by finding an implied right to abortion in the Fourteenth Amendment's right to privacy, which critics, including many legal scholars who support abortion rights, saw as weak reasoning and judicial overreach that took the issue away from democratic debate. Supporters saw it as protecting reproductive freedom and health, so the decision was contested on both moral and constitutional grounds until it was overturned in 2022 by Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization.
